scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router2 RIP version
Mechanism: router0 and router1 run RIPv2; router2 was switched
  to RIPv1. The two versions use different packet formats and
  v2 peers drop v1 updates by default (and vice versa). router2
  is "sending" updates that router1 ignores. router2's own
  connected networks stay in its RIB; only advertised ones
  vanish elsewhere.
Localization: router2
Root cause: RIP version mismatch (router2 v1, neighbors v2)
Fix: `vtysh -c "router rip" -c "version 2"` on router2

agent.diagnosis_text:
After a config change, router2's RIP daemon was set to "version 1"
(RIPv1). This controls both the send format (RIPv1 broadcast to
255.255.255.255) and, critically, the receive filter ("receive version
1"). Meanwhile, router1 remained configured with "version 2", which
locks both its send format (RIPv2 multicast to 224.0.0.9) and its
receive filter to RIPv2 only.

The consequence is a one-way version mismatch on the wan_r1_r2 link
(router1.eth3 / router2.eth2). Every RIPv1 broadcast that router2
sends is counted as a bad packet by router1 (BadPackets = 3 for peer
20.20.0.2 confirmed in "show ip rip status"), because router1's
receive filter strictly rejects version-1 headers. With no valid
incoming update refreshing the route entries, the RIP 180-second
expiry timer runs to zero and the routes 1.0.0.0/8 and 128.168.0.0/16
(router2's directly connected networks) are flushed from router1's
table. They reappear only if a stray acceptable packet is processed,
giving the intermittent symptom the user observed. Router2 believes
it is sending correctly (its own routes appear as C(i) self-sourced
in "show ip rip"), which matches the report that "router2 reports it's
sending updates but nobody receives them."

Root cause: The post-change "version 1" directive in router2's RIP
configuration makes its updates incompatible with router1's strict
"receive version 2" policy.

Fix: On router2, change the RIP global version directive from
"version 1" to "version 2" so both routers use RIPv2 send/receive,
restoring compatible multicast-based updates across the WAN link.

per_axis.rationale: The writeup explicitly names router2 as the device running RIPv1 and the location requiring the version change.
The diagnosis explicitly names a RIP version/protocol mismatch—router2 running RIPv1 while its neighbors run RIPv2—as the root cause.
Recommends changing router2's RIP global version from 1 to 2, which matches the expected fix and restores RIPv2 compatibility.

The agent ran appropriate show commands (running-config, show ip rip/status) and recorded concrete observations (RIP version mismatch and BadPackets counts) which support the conclusion. The reasoning that v1/v2 mismatch causes dropped updates and route expiry is direct and correctly links evidence to root cause and fix.
